investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-20T21:40–21:48Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the 6-node cluster has only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which are already at capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a remote state value, causing all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to be absent and the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler cannot place the remote-agent pod because the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is exhausted on the only 2 eligible nodes (both report "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm") and the other 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption is also unavailable. The pod remains Unschedulable for the full eval window (~130–146 s), so createAgent() in run-status-probes.mjs never returns a live agent, and the eval produces an empty evidence object, violating the contract defined in check-expectations.json lines 256–259.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: concurrent workloads or a prior eval run that did not clean up have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new pods.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a label or taint (e.g. kata-containers or peer-pods node label) that only 2 nodes carry, so the schedulable pool is structurally limited to 2 nodes regardless of overall cluster size.

TERTIARY — Leaked/zombie remote-agent VMs from a previous eval run holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if withCleanup() in run-status-probes.mjs did not complete cleanup on a prior failure, those VM resource allocations may still be counted against node capacity.

QUATERNARY — Cluster under-provisioned for concurrent eval load: the 2 kata-capable nodes may have a resource limit of 1 VM each, making the effective concurrency ceiling 2; if multiple eval runs or product workloads compete simultaneously, exhaustion is expected.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-20T21:43–21:48Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes have no remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the eval runner calls createAgent with type "remote" (run-status-probes.mjs:1905) before it can poll state, the pod never schedules, no agent is created, and the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are never written — causing the contract validation to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that label. The remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on those 2 nodes. As a result, every new remote-agent pod submitted by the eval runner is stuck Unschedulable, the agent is never created, and the eval probe never reaches the state-polling step — so all required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) is absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Kubernetes node pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

With 0/6 nodes available for scheduling and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure that prevents the eval runner from provisioning any remote agent, causing all downstream evidence collection and contract assertions to fail. This is an eval-observed infrastructure failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to production end-users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-20T21:40–21:48Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the 6-node cluster has only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which are already at capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a remote state value, causing all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) to be absent and the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler cannot place the remote-agent pod because the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is exhausted on the only 2 eligible nodes (both report "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm") and the other 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption is also unavailable. The pod remains Unschedulable for the full eval window (~130–146 s), so createAgent() in run-status-probes.mjs never returns a live agent, and the eval produces an empty evidence object, violating the contract defined in check-expectations.json lines 256–259.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message, latencyMs=149750, endedAt=2026-06-20T21:48:05.053Z

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent===true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready']
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=133877, well within the outageLatencyMs=360000 threshold, so the failure is a scheduling block not a timeout
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: concurrent workloads or a prior eval run that did not clean up have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new pods.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a label or taint (e.g. kata-containers or peer-pods node label) that only 2 nodes carry, so the schedulable pool is structurally limited to 2 nodes regardless of overall cluster size.

TERTIARY — Leaked/zombie remote-agent VMs from a previous eval run holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if withCleanup() in run-status-probes.mjs did not complete cleanup on a prior failure, those VM resource allocations may still be counted against node capacity.

QUATERNARY — Cluster under-provisioned for concurrent eval load: the 2 kata-capable nodes may have a resource limit of 1 VM each, making the effective concurrency ceiling 2; if multiple eval runs or product workloads compete simultaneously, exhaustion is expected.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-20T21:43–21:48Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes have no remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the eval runner calls createAgent with type "remote" (run-status-probes.mjs:1905) before it can poll state, the pod never schedules, no agent is created, and the required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are never written — causing the contract validation to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that label. The remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on those 2 nodes. As a result, every new remote-agent pod submitted by the eval runner is stuck Unschedulable, the agent is never created, and the eval probe never reaches the state-polling step — so all required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) is absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Kubernetes node pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
